transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-03
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Marcus Hale (Seabreeze Head of ML), Rina Patel (Platform Eng), Samir Khan (CTO)

Summary (auto): quick optimize walkthrough focusing on batching and cache patterns, cost modeling for a payments chatbot across short/long contexts. Customer concerns: latency SLO 200-300ms tail, sensitive PII, SOC2 compliance, prefer VPC/private deployment for initial pilot.

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm alex from redwood, with priya who is our solutions eng, we'll run through optimize recommendations for batching and prefix/KV cache and then walk the cost model. sound good?
[00:12] Marcus: yep, thanks. quick context — we're building a payments assistant, most sessions are short single-turn queries but some multi-step auth flows reach 800 tokens. we care a lot about tail latency and cost, and we have PCI restrictions so private deployment is likely.
[00:30] Priya: great, that helps. i'll start with batching concepts then show how prefix cache (we sometimes call it prefetch) vs kv-cache behave, and then we'll map that to cost per 1M requests. note — some transcribed terms might be off, e.g., we say kv cache and kv-cache interchangeably.
[00:50] Priya: first, batching. redwood's runtime can do continuous batching which groups in-flight requests for the same model variant. for short responses batching increases throughput and reduces per-token GPU cost, but adds a bit of latency depending on your batching window.
[01:10] Rina: can you quantify that? we need 99th percentile < 300ms for auth flows.
[01:18] Priya: yes. in our benchmarks, micro-batch sizes of 4-8 for short prompts add ~10-30ms p99 but can cut token cost by 20-40% compared to single-request execution. important caveat: for very bursty traffic you can configure max-latency SLO to cap batch wait.
[01:40] Alex: also routing policy: you can route by latency tier — high-priority requests skip large batching and go to a lower-latency pool (dedicated) while background requests use larger batches on cheaper capacity.
[01:52] Samir: sounds like a good knob. how does cache fit in — prefix vs kv?
[01:58] Priya: prefix cache is best when many requests share initial prompts or templates — we store prefix key states and re-use KV cache within the same model run to avoid re-computing the early layers. kv-cache here means the per-token KV key/value cache for autoregressive decoders; our 'prefix caching' store saves commonly-seen prefixes and their KV state so we can fast-path generation.
[02:22] Marcus: hm, our messages vary but we do a lot of similar system prompts and templates for authentication. could be a good fit.
[02:30] Priya: right — typical tradeoffs: prefix cache reduces compute for tokens in the cached prefix so it lowers p99 and cost, but it has storage and invalidation overhead. KV cache during a session reduces repeated computation for long contexts, especially helpful for multi-turn flows — you avoid recomputing the full context each step.
[02:52] Rina: what about hit rates? our flows are semi-structured; what hit rates should we expect?
[02:58] Priya: depends. for templated system prompts we see 70-90% prefix hit rates in some finserv customers; general user messages much lower. for KV cache in session, hit rate is effectively 100% for tokens after it's warmed (it's per-session), so it's more about session length distribution.
[03:18] Alex: i'll show a quick cost example. assume model cost X GPU per hour; with batching and good prefix hits you can reduce per-request token compute by ~30-50%. so if current hosted cost is $Y per 1M tokens, optimize can bring it down to ~0.6Y or lower depending on cache hit and batch sizes.
[03:38] Samir: can you show the spreadsheet?
[03:40] Alex: yes sending the spreadsheet after. (links) — "Optimize cost model - example".

[03:50] Priya: demo time — here's a sample flow. i'm running two variants: full context no caching vs prefix cached + batch size 8. i'll stream results.
[04:02] [04:02] Priya (demo): launching, note the demo infra is on a smaller instance so numbers are illustrative.
[04:18] Priya: you can see p50/p95 improve when we use prefix cache and batching for repeated templates — p95 drops from ~420ms to ~260ms in this demo. numbers vary in production but directionally similar.
[04:35] Marcus: 260ms p95 is promising. our SLA is 300ms. how do we ensure tail isn't affected by cold starts or evictions?
[04:44] Priya: we recommend a warm pool for critical routes — keep minimum reserved workers and use dedicated capacity for the highest-priority traffic. also automatic fallback: when a prefix cache miss occurs we can fallback to a compatible model variant or reduce batch size to preserve latency.
[05:02] Rina: any security concerns storing prefix states? we can't store PII.
[05:08] Alex: good callout. prefix cache can be configured to exclude user-identifying tokens and we support encryption at rest (KMS). for private deployments we can keep caches inside the customer's VPC and use customer-managed keys. we'll share SOC2 and encryption docs.
[05:26] Samir: re: private deployment — what's the onboarding timeline for a pilot?
[05:30] Alex: typically 2-3 weeks to provision dev cluster + pilot run, depending on approvals. for VPC/private we do a security review which can add time.
[05:40] Priya: back to cost model, key inputs are: request size distribution (tokens in/out), session length distribution, expected prefix hit rate, batch window/latency SLO, and model variant selection (fp16 vs quantized). we provided a spreadsheet template that takes those inputs and produces per-million-request cost and latency percentiles.
[06:02] Marcus: about quantization — do you recommend 4-bit for finance? any quality regression risk?
[06:08] Priya: quantization (4-bit/8-bit) reduces GPU memory and can increase throughput. we recommend validating on your eval set; Redwood Optimize flags potential regressions and suggests fallback to higher-precision variants for critical routes. for many llm workloads quality hit is minimal, but must be validated.
[06:26] Marcus: ok, we'll run our prompt evaluation.
[06:30] [06:30] Alex: Okay, i'll recap requirements i heard: 1) pilot in private VPC for payments assistant, 2) p99 target ~300ms, 3) evaluate cost model vs your on-prem baseline, 4) security review (SOC2 docs, KMS config).
[06:45] Samir: yes that's accurate. also want to include compliance folks in the security review.
[06:50] Alex: great. next steps i flagged in the action items. we'll send pricing and the cost model spreadsheet.
[07:00] Rina: one more technical Q — what about warm KV cache eviction policies when memory pressure hits?
[07:07] Priya: eviction is LRU with configurable TTL and size limits; for private clusters you can increase memory allocation for cache. we also support partial caching for prefixes above a size threshold.
[07:20] Marcus: what's the expected storage footprint for prefix cache at 100k distinct templates?
[07:26] Priya: ballpark depends on kv-state size per prefix — for mid-sized models maybe 2-8MB per prefix, so 100k could be large; most customers store only top 5-10k prefixes and use TTL. we can run sizing estimates in the pilot.
[07:40] Samir: good to know.
[07:44] Alex: ok let's go through the concrete next steps and owners now.
[07:48] Priya: action items repeated: we'll share slides/spreadsheet; alex will send pricing options including dedicated capacity and burst policies; seabr— seabreeze will confirm pilot infra and security contacts.
[08:00] Marcus: timeline — we aim to have pilot infra ready by 6/10 and run pilot week of 6/15.
[08:06] Alex: cool. anything else?
[08:09] Rina: one small ask: include example A/B thresholds for quality regression monitoring in the slides.
[08:14] Priya: will do — Optimize has built-in eval hooks that can trigger alerts on regression for specific prompt sets.
[08:22] Samir: thanks, that's all from me.
[08:25] Alex: great — thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the deck, cost sheet, security docs, and proposed pilot schedule.

End transcript.

Notes on transcript quality: medium — occasional mis-attribution, some product names transcribed as "pre-fetch" or "pre-fix cache". Natural speech, some filler words removed and some short timestamps approximated.
notes: Customer is pilot-ready; primary blockers: security review and infra access. Strong fit for dedicated capacity + prefix caching for templated auth flows. Recommend pilot with 2-week benchmark focusing on p95/p99 and cost per 1M requests.
